decisions.question: Why use CSS custom properties (variables) for the design system?
decisions.answer: CSS variables centralize all design tokens (colors, spacing, radii, transitions) for consistency across future screens. Makes it easy for subsequent stories to reuse the same tokens without hardcoding values.

decisions.question: Why use an IIFE in app.js instead of ES modules?
decisions.answer: The project uses vanilla JS without a bundler. An IIFE avoids polluting the global scope while keeping compatibility simple. No need for module syntax since there's only one JS file.

decisions.question: Why include a placeholder screen-1 in index.html already?
decisions.answer: The CTA on the welcome screen navigates to screen 1. Including a minimal placeholder ensures the navigation works correctly for US-001 verification, and US-002 will flesh it out with the full form engine.

decisions.question: Why use TOTAL_STEPS=7 instead of 8?
decisions.answer: The PRD says '8 total steps' but screen 0 is welcome and screen 8 is thank-you — neither are questionnaire steps. The 7 actual questionnaire screens (1-7) are what the progress bar tracks. Progress = currentScreen/7 * 100.

decisions.question: Why auto-advance choice cards with a 300ms delay?
decisions.answer: Instant advance feels jarring — users don't see their selection. A 300ms delay gives visual feedback (the card highlights with gold border/tint) before sliding to the next screen, creating a Heyflow-like premium feel.

decisions.question: Why use MutationObserver to restore choice selections on back-navigation?
decisions.answer: When navigating back, the screen gets the screen--active class. A MutationObserver watching class changes on the form container detects this and restores the previously-selected card from state.answers. This avoids coupling the restoration logic into goToScreen.

decisions.question: Why use requestAnimationFrame for focus management after transitions?
decisions.answer: After goToScreen sets the target screen to active, the browser needs a frame to apply the CSS transition. Using requestAnimationFrame ensures the focus call happens after the screen is visible, avoiding focus on hidden elements.

decisions.question: Why use inline SVG icons instead of an icon font or external images?
decisions.answer: Inline SVGs have zero external dependencies (matching the project constraint), are stylable via CSS currentColor for seamless color transitions on hover/selection, and render crisply at any size. They follow the existing pattern of inline SVGs used for button arrows.

decisions.question: Why use delegated input events for clearing validation errors?
decisions.answer: A single 'input' event listener on formContainer handles all fields via event delegation. This avoids attaching individual listeners to each textarea/input and automatically works for any future fields added to the form.

decisions.question: Why use max-height transition for error messages instead of display:none?
decisions.answer: display:none cannot be animated. Using opacity + max-height creates a smooth reveal/hide animation for validation error messages, matching the premium feel of the rest of the UI. The max-height: 2em is enough for a single-line error.

decisions.question: Why use side-by-side visual choice cards instead of a range slider for screen 4?
decisions.answer: A range slider (input[type=range]) is hard to style consistently across browsers, has poor touch accessibility, and doesn't map well to a binary choice. Two large visual cards side-by-side give clear tap targets on mobile, immediate visual feedback via the existing choice-card--selected state, and match the premium Heyflow-style aesthetic. They also reuse the existing auto-advance JS pattern.

decisions.question: Why add hint text below the label on visual choice cards?
decisions.answer: The two visual choices (Spontaneous Adventure vs Planned Evening) benefit from a short descriptor to help users decide. The hint text uses --color-text-muted and transitions to --color-gold-light on selection, maintaining the premium feel without cluttering the card.

decisions.question: Why use a centralized handlePhotoFile() function for both click and drag-drop?
decisions.answer: Both click-to-upload and drag-drop produce a File object. A single handlePhotoFile() handles validation (5MB limit, image type check) and FileReader preview in one place, avoiding duplicated logic between the two input paths.

decisions.question: Why store the photo data URL on state._photoDataUrl?
decisions.answer: When the user navigates back to screen 6, the MutationObserver restores the preview by setting previewImg.src from state._photoDataUrl. Without storing it, the preview would be lost since the FileReader result is ephemeral. The underscore prefix signals it's internal state, not a user answer.

decisions.question: Why use role='button' and tabindex='0' on the upload area instead of a native button?
decisions.answer: The upload area is a div that acts as a click/drag target. Adding role='button' + tabindex='0' makes it keyboard-accessible and announces correctly to screen readers. A native button wouldn't support drag-drop or the visual layout needed for the drop zone.
